title.narrative: ROAP/RAS/M1-323/WATER FOR LIFE CAMPAIGN IN ASIA AND THE PACIFIC (PHASE II)

description.narrative: The rapid economic growth, urbanization, and population increase in many cities across Asia and the Pacific have outpaced the provision of essential infrastructure, services, and supplies, including water, sanitation, and food. This rapid and often unplanned growth has placed immense pressure on the environment, further limiting access to safe and secure water and sanitation for vulnerable populations. While this project primarily focuses on addressing water-related challenges in rapidly urbanizing areas, it also emphasizes generating positive synergies in related areas such as gender equality, food security, education, technology application, and capacity building. By integrating these interconnected issues, the project seeks to create comprehensive solutions that alleviate environmental and social pressures while enhancing the overall well-being and resilience of the region’s most vulnerable communities. The project embraces the latest advancements in global technology and know-how, particularly from Japan, to deliver efficient and sustainable solutions to urban challenges in Asia. It specifically aims to bridge the gap between innovative solutions emerging in Japan and the urgent needs of fast-growing cities in the region. By identifying, adapting, and introducing effective technologies and expertise—especially from Japanese small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs)—that have successfully tackled similar environmental challenges, the initiative ensures that each intervention is practical, culturally relevant, and tailored to meet community-specific needs. In addition to improving access to basic urban services, the project provides SMEs with the opportunity to pilot, scale, and adapt technologies that address various development issues directly on the ground. By partnering with a diverse network of partners, including central and local governments, universities, NGOs (such as women’s organizations), schools, and communities, with support from Japanese local governments (such as those in Fukuoka and Kyushu), private sector technology firms, academic institutions, and UN-Habitat country offices, the project fosters a collaborative approach that aligns the latest sustainable technologies with the development challenges facing Asian cities to create a lasting, transformative improvements through technical solutions in access to basic services, environmental sustainability, and urban resilience in vulnerable communities across Asia and the Pacific, while establishing a smooth channel for public and private partnerships. Expected outcomes: • Augmented knowledge and capacity within targeted UN-Habitat partner communities to plan and pilot innovative WASH and other urban basic services solutions. • Sustained partnership mobilization in Japan for the promotion of innovative solutions in the Asia and the Pacific. Expected outputs: • knowledge and capacity building activities held for enhancing local capacity in utilizing relevant technologies in Nepal • community plans and pilot projects created in targeted communities in Nepal • knowledge and capacity building activities held for enhancing local capacity in utilizing relevant technologies in Laos • community plans and pilot projects created in targeted communities in Laos • outreach activities to promote UN-Habitat low-cost solutions through different media channels • new partnership set up in Japan
